h1: Electrical Service and Meter Upgrades in Broward County
intro: Sometimes the problem is not one panel or one breaker, it is the whole electrical service showing its age at once. The mast is corroded, the meter socket is failing, the disconnect is tired, and patching any single piece just moves the trouble along. That is when a service upgrade is the honest answer. We rebuild the service entrance as a whole, the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the grounding, and the panel when it is part of the job, for homes and commercial properties. When it is only the meter socket, we handle that too. We forecast the entire job and price it once before we begin. For most homes a rebuild runs $5,000 to $8,000 depending on condition and scope, and we tell you where yours lands before work starts.

definition.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is
definition.body: An electrical service and meter upgrade is the removal and replacement of the parts that bring power into your property and distribute it, from the utility connection to the panel. The service is everything on that path: the mast and riser where the line meets the building, the meter socket that holds the utility's meter, the main disconnect that shuts the building down, the grounding, and the panel or panels that divide power into circuits. Over time these pieces age together, and when enough of them are worn or obsolete, replacing them one at a time is slower and costlier than doing the job right in one pass. An upgrade can be the whole service rebuilt as a unit, or a single piece like the meter socket when that is all that has failed. Either way, it is brought up to current code, sized correctly, and left working together. This is the core of what Ghost Crown Electric does, for both residential and commercial properties.

symptoms.title: Multiple parts of the service are failing
symptoms.body: It is not just the panel. The meter socket is worn, the disconnect is tired, and the panel is obsolete all at once. When several pieces are near the end together, upgrading the service as a whole is more honest than chasing one failure at a time.

symptoms.title: Your insurer wants the service updated
symptoms.body: A 4-point inspection or a carrier flagged the electrical service, not just the panel. In South Florida this pushes many owners toward a full upgrade, because bringing the whole service to current code is what satisfies the inspection cleanly.

symptoms.title: The meter socket or mast is damaged
symptoms.body: The meter housing, the mast, or the point where power enters the building is corroded, loose, scorched, or pulling away, or the utility red-tagged the meter. That is the front door of your electrical system, and damage there often means the service behind it needs work too.

symptoms.title: Repeated repairs that never quite hold
symptoms.body: You have paid for one electrical fix after another and the trouble keeps returning somewhere new. When patching stops solving the problem, it usually means the service itself has aged out and wants replacing as a whole.

symptoms.title: The service is undersized for the property
symptoms.body: The building asks more of the electrical service than it was ever built to give, and the panel is full with nowhere to grow. An undersized, maxed out service is a candidate for an upgrade sized for how the property actually lives now.

symptoms.title: Heat, scorching, or a burning smell at the service
symptoms.body: You feel warmth, see scorching, or catch a burning smell around the meter, the disconnect, or the panel. Electricity is something we do not see, we only feel the effect. Those effects across the service point to wear that an upgrade resolves for good.

localSections.heading: Aging services in South Florida housing
localSections.body: Broward County grew in waves across many decades, and each wave installed electrical services built for the electrical life of its time. A service that was generous in its era can be undersized and worn now, after decades of added air conditioning, appliances, and the general growth in how a home uses power. When we open an older service from West Palm Beach down to North Miami Beach, it is common to find the mast, the meter socket, the panel, and the disconnect all aging together, because they went in together and have lived the same years. The climate is hard on all of it. The service lives partly outside, so sun and heat wear on the enclosures, humidity works into the meter housing, and homes near the coast face salt air that corrodes the meter socket, the lugs, and the terminations. Corrosion and heat feed on each other and can quietly compromise the whole assembly, not just one part. That is exactly the situation where a full upgrade makes more sense than repairing one piece and waiting for the next to go.

localSections.heading: How carriers view the electrical service
localSections.body: South Florida insurance carriers scrutinize the electrical service closely, and their concern often reaches beyond a single obsolete panel. A 4-point inspection reports on the electrical system as a whole, and an aging or undersized service, worn meter equipment, or an obsolete panel can each contribute to a failed electrical section. Some carriers decline a new policy over it, and others drop a renewal on a home they have covered for years. This is honest, verifiable reality in the current market, and it is why many owners find that repairing one piece is not enough to clear the objection. A full upgrade that brings the entire service to current code addresses the whole electrical section at once. We handle the permit and we meet the inspector, so you get clean documentation for your carrier. Then the electrical reason your policy was in question is resolved thoroughly, in a way that holds up at the next renewal too.

guide.title: The complete guide to electrical service and meter upgrades in South Florida

sections.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is and when you need one
sections.body: Your electrical service is the whole path power takes from the utility into your building and out to your circuits. It includes the mast and riser where the utility line meets the building, the meter socket where power is measured, the main disconnect that shuts the building down, the panel or panels that divide power into circuits, and the grounding that ties the whole thing to earth. A service and meter upgrade is the removal and replacement of that system, in whole or in the parts that have aged out. You need the full job when enough of the service has worn out that fixing a single piece no longer makes sense. If the panel is obsolete, the meter socket is corroded, and the disconnect is tired all at the same time, replacing them one at a time is slower, more disruptive, and in the end more expensive than doing it right in one pass. A rebuild brings everything up to current code together, sized for how the property actually uses power today. This is the core of what Ghost Crown Electric does, for homes and commercial properties, and it is an in and out type of situation. That is what we do.

sections.heading: How we forecast the job, and what it costs
sections.body: The single most important promise on a service upgrade is the price, and here is how we handle it. We do not quote from a phone call or a photograph, because we would only be guessing, and a guess is not a price you can trust. We come to the property and assess the whole service in person: the mast, the meter socket, the disconnect, the panels, the grounding, and the condition of every connection. Then we forecast what the job actually takes and give you one number before any work begins, and that number does not change halfway through. For most residential properties, an electrical service rebuild runs $5,000 to $8,000, depending on the condition of the existing service and the scope of the work. A service that is worn but straightforward sits lower in that range, and one that needs more extensive work across the meter, the disconnect, and the distribution sits higher. Commercial properties vary more and are quoted per situation after we see them. Separate from a rebuild, our standard service call is $240, which covers roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and diagnosis, and if a smaller problem can be handled on the spot, there is no separate return charge. Price it once, price it right.

sections.heading: When it is just the meter socket
sections.body: Sometimes the service as a whole is sound and the trouble is only the meter socket, the box where the utility's meter plugs into your building. It takes the full brunt of South Florida weather, so it shows up with rust streaks, a cracked or loose enclosure, scorch marks, or a meter that sits crooked. Left alone, a failing socket can arc, overheat, or drop power to the whole property, because everything downstream runs through it. Replacing it is not a job for a handyman and not a job to do without the power company, because the utility owns the meter and has to disconnect and reconnect it on a scheduled window. We handle that coordination with the utility, pull the permit, do the work with our own crew, meet the inspector, and time everything so your power is off for the shortest safe period. If the utility has red-tagged the meter and will not reconnect until it is fixed, that is exactly the situation we manage from start to finish. And if we open things up and find the failure has spread to the disconnect or the panel behind the socket, we will show you honestly what we see before we go any further.

sections.heading: What the day of the work looks like
sections.body: An electrical service upgrade is a coordinated job, and we plan it so your time without power is as short and predictable as it can be. It is an in and out type of situation. That is what we do. We arrange with the utility so power to the property can be interrupted safely for the work window, and we tell you honestly ahead of time what to expect so you can plan around it. Then our three-person in-house crew removes the old service and rebuilds it as a unit: the mast and riser, the meter socket, the disconnect, the panel or panels, and the grounding, reconnecting and labeling every circuit as we go. Because we run three trucks and can work three jobs at once, we staff the job properly rather than stretching one person thin. When the work is complete, we schedule the county inspection so the whole system is verified and documented before we consider the job finished. Before the day arrives, there is little you need to do beyond clearing access to the meter, the disconnect, and the panels, and making a plan for the stretch without power. If your household works from home or depends on medical equipment, or the property is a business that cannot simply go dark, tell us early so we can schedule the window to fit. We would rather build the day around your life than ask you to build your life around ours.

sections.heading: How to choose a contractor for a job this size
sections.body: A service upgrade is one of the larger electrical jobs a property owner will ever authorize, so the contractor matters as much as the work. Start with licensing. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor with statewide authority and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Ask whether the contractor pulls the permit in their own name and who attends the inspection, because on a service job the documentation and the sign-off are as important as the equipment. Ask whether the company coordinates the utility disconnect and reconnect, because that handoff is where an unlicensed hand tends to get stuck. Ask who does the work, since an in-house crew that rebuilds services routinely is not the same as subcontractors assembled for one job. And be wary of anyone who wins your trust by running down every other company. We do not do that. We let the license and the record speak, we give a customer more than what they pay for, and we show up when we say we will. On a job this size, that reliability is the thing you are actually buying, along with a forecast that comes from ten years of services already seen and solved.

faqs.question: What exactly is included in a service and meter upgrade?
faqs.answer: It covers the electrical service as a system: the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the grounding, and the panel or panels when they are part of the job. Rather than fixing one worn part and waiting for the next to fail, we bring the service up to current code, sized for how your property actually uses power today. It is the core of what we do.

faqs.question: How much does a service and meter upgrade cost?
faqs.answer: For most residential properties, a rebuild runs $5,000 to $8,000, depending on the condition of the existing service and the scope of the work. Commercial properties are quoted per situation, and a single meter socket replacement is quoted per property. We forecast the whole job and give you one price before we start, and it does not change mid-job. Our standard service call is $240, which covers roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can you just replace the meter socket, or does it have to be the whole service?
faqs.answer: We do both. If the service is otherwise sound and only the meter socket has failed, we replace the socket by itself and coordinate the utility disconnect and reconnect and the permit as one clean job. If we find the failure has spread to the disconnect, the panel, or the conductors behind it, we will show you honestly what we see and let you decide. We do not sell a full upgrade to a property that only needs the socket.

faqs.question: Will the price really not change once you start?
faqs.answer: Correct. We forecast the entire job in person before we quote it, so the number we give you is the number. Price it once, price it right. We do not come back partway through asking for more, because getting the forecast right the first time is our responsibility. Ten years of situations already seen is what lets us price a service job accurately up front.

faqs.question: Do I need a full upgrade, or just a repair?
faqs.answer: It depends on what we find, and we will tell you honestly. Many problems are a single repair or a single part like the meter socket, and if that is what your property needs, that is what we will recommend. A full upgrade makes sense when several parts of the service are worn at once, when repeated repairs keep failing, or when an inspection flagged the whole electrical system. We stay in our lane and do not oversell.

faqs.question: How long will my power be off during the work?
faqs.answer: For part of the work, since replacing the service means interrupting the power that feeds it. We coordinate with the utility and tell you honestly ahead of time what to expect so you can plan around it. Because we run three trucks and staff the job properly with our own crew, it is a focused, in and out type of situation rather than a job that drags on for days.
